deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a continuous prose passage of German lecture or study notes on Greek history. It continues from folio 98, which covered Coronea, Cnidus, Conon and the Peace of Antalcidas in 387, and it runs on to folio 100 (Epaminondas, Pelopidas, the liberation of Thebes). The content is:

(1) Among the Greek colonies, Olynthus was the most powerful. It oppressed the others, so they allied and appealed to Sparta (marginal date 383).

(2) The Spartans sent an army to Macedonia/Chalcidice to take up the cause of the other towns. The war lasted into its third year and ended with the defeat of Olynthus.

(3) During this expedition the Spartans committed an act of arrogance. Marching through Boeotia, they seized Thebes by surprise and installed a garrison. Their commander Phoebidas carried this out in 382.

(4) A government like the Thirty Tyrants at Athens was set up in Thebes. It oppressed the Thebans so harshly that all the propertied citizens emigrated.

(5) Two men, Epaminondas and Pelopidas, arose to avenge their city on Sparta. They are called 'the two greatest characters in Greek history'. It is noted to their credit that no quarrel ever arose between them while they led the state, and that they were friends from youth onward.

There is no derivation, formula or computation to reconstruct. The page also gives no internal evidence of Gauss's authorship (hand, subject matter). It may be notes by another person filed in this bundle, though this cannot be decided from the page alone.
errors: Historical simplification: the appeal to Sparta came from Acanthus and Apollonia against the Chalcidian League led by Olynthus. Ancient sources date it to 383/382 BC, so the date 383 is acceptable.
The Olynthian War is usually dated 382-379 BC. 'Into the third year' is consistent with this.

Phoebidas' seizure of the Cadmea (382 BC) is described as seizing 'the city of Thebes'. Strictly it was the citadel, taken with the help of the pro-Spartan faction under Leontiades. This is a minor simplification, not an error.
There are no mathematical errors because there is no mathematics.

results.what: Narrative notes on Greek history (the Olynthian War, the Spartan seizure of Thebes in 382 BC, the introduction of Epaminondas and Pelopidas)
results.modern_name: Not mathematics; standard school/lecture history of Greece (Xenophon's Hellenica, Plutarch's Pelopidas, Nepos)
results.usually_credited_to: Ancient historians (Xenophon, Plutarch, Diodorus); standard textbook material c. 1800

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine historical lecture or study notes with no mathematical content. Nothing here bears on Gauss's mathematical work, and authorship by Gauss himself is not evident from the page.

checkable.asserts: An Olynthian War from 382 to 379 BC lasts into its third year, consistent with 'bis ins 3 Jahr'.
Five years separate the Peace of Antalcidas (387, previous page) and Phoebidas' seizure of Thebes (382).

transcription_corrections: Line 5: 'um sie sich[?] der übrigen Städte einnehmen[?]' is more plausibly 'um sich der übrigen Städte anzunehmen / annehmen', i.e. to take up the cause of the remaining towns.
'in der griechischen Geschichte' and 'die 2 größten Charaktere' are confirmed by the image.
The struck-out words after 'dass' appear to be 'sie, solo' (cancelled), then 'unter ihnen, so lange'. In 'nie ein Streit [-unter-] ihnen entstand' the cancelled word is 'unter'.
The year after 'Phoebidas aus' reads '382', confirmed. The marginal date after 'wandten' reads '383', confirmed.
